easy.def: The part of your head that thinks.
examples: Your brain helps you learn.
The brain tells your body what to do.
A brain is in your head.

more.def: The organ inside your head that controls your body and lets you think, feel and remember.
examples: Your brain sends messages to every part of your body.
Reading exercises your brain.
Humans have large brains compared to their size.

easy.def: The part that makes a bike or car stop.
examples: I pressed the brake.
The bike has a brake.
The brake squeaked.

more.def: The part of a bike or car that slows it down or stops it.
examples: He pressed the brake and the car stopped.
The brakes on my bike squeak.
Dad checked the brakes before the trip.

easy.def: To slow down or stop.
examples: The driver braked hard.
I brake at the corner.
The car braked.

more.def: To slow down or stop a vehicle by pressing the pedal or lever.
examples: The driver braked when the light turned red.
I braked at the bottom of the hill.
The bus braked quickly to avoid the dog.

easy.def: A part of a tree that grows out from the trunk.
examples: The bird sat on a branch.
The branch is long.
A branch fell off the tree.

more.def: One of the woody parts of a tree that grows out from the trunk.
examples: The bird perched on a branch.
The wind snapped a dry branch from the tree.
The children climbed along a thick branch.

easy.def: One part of a larger group or business.
examples: The bank has a branch downtown.
The library has a branch in our town.
We visited a branch of the library.

more.def: One of the offices or shops that belongs to a larger group.
examples: The bank has a branch near my school.
The library has a branch in every neighborhood.
The company opened a new branch.

easy.def: A name that a company gives to its products.
examples: What brand of cereal do you eat?
My shoes are a good brand.
That brand is popular.

more.def: A name or mark that a company gives to the things it makes.
examples: What brand of cereal do you like?
He wore shoes of a popular brand.
The store sells many brands of juice.

easy.def: Not letting fear stop you.
examples: The brave girl went down the big slide.
The brave boy got his shot at the doctor.
Firefighters are brave.

more.def: Willing to do something hard or scary even when you feel afraid.
examples: It was brave of him to speak in front of the whole school.
The brave sailor steered the ship through the storm.
She was brave enough to say sorry first.

easy.def: A soft food that you cut in slices.
examples: I made a sandwich with bread.
The bread is warm.
We ate bread and soup.

more.def: A food made by baking flour, water and yeast, often cut into slices.
examples: The smell of fresh bread filled the kitchen.
Bakers get up early to make bread before the shop opens.
Toast is bread that has been heated until it is crisp.

easy.def: To come apart in pieces.
examples: The glass can break.
I broke a plate.
The stick is broken.

more.def: To come apart or make something come apart, often by hitting or dropping it.
examples: Be careful, or the glass will break on the hard floor.
The toy broke when it fell down the stairs.
He broke the chocolate bar into four pieces.

easy.def: A short time to rest.
examples: We take a break.
It is time for a break.
Let us have a break.

more.def: A short rest from work or study.
examples: The class took a break to stretch and drink water.
We stopped for a break halfway up the mountain.
There is no school during the winter break.

easy.def: The first meal of the day.
examples: I eat breakfast at seven.
We have eggs for breakfast.
Breakfast is ready.

more.def: The meal that you eat in the morning.
examples: We had pancakes for breakfast.
She skipped breakfast and ran for the bus.
Breakfast is the first meal of the day.

easy.def: The air you take in and let out.
examples: Take a deep breath.
I held my breath.
I lost my breath.

more.def: The air that goes in and out of your lungs.
examples: Take a deep breath and count to ten.
He held his breath under water.
She ran so fast she lost her breath.

easy.def: To take air in and let it out.
examples: We breathe air.
Breathe in slowly.
Fish do not breathe air.

more.def: To take air into the body and send it out again.
examples: Take a deep breath and breathe out slowly.
Whales breathe through a hole on top of their heads.
It was hard to breathe at the top of the mountain.

easy.def: A soft wind.
examples: A cool breeze blew my hair.
The breeze moved the curtains.
My kite flew in the breeze.

more.def: A light, gentle wind.
examples: A breeze from the sea kept us cool on the hot beach.
The flags waved gently in the morning breeze.
We opened the windows to let the breeze in.

easy.def: A hard block used to build walls.
examples: The house is made of brick.
The brick is red.
I built a wall of brick.

more.def: A hard block of baked clay, used to build walls and houses.
examples: The wall was built of red brick.
The builder laid bricks one by one.
A brick fell off the old chimney.

easy.def: A woman who is getting married.
examples: The bride wore a white dress.
The bride and groom smiled.
The bride carried flowers.

more.def: A woman on her wedding day, or just married.
examples: The bride walked down the aisle with her father.
Guests threw petals as the bride and groom left.
The bride wore a long veil.

easy.def: A road over water or a gap.
examples: We drove over the bridge.
The bridge is high.
A train crossed the bridge.

more.def: A structure built over a river, road or gap so people can cross it.
examples: We walked across the bridge over the river.
A long bridge connects the island to the land.
The old bridge was made of wood.

easy.def: Short.
examples: It was a brief talk.
The visit was brief.
She gave a brief speech.

more.def: Lasting only a short time, or using only a few words.
examples: The teacher gave a brief talk.
We took a brief break.
After a brief rest, we kept walking.

easy.def: Full of light.
examples: The sun is very bright.
I wear a bright yellow coat.
The lamp is too bright for my eyes.

more.def: Giving off or filled with a lot of light; also, strong in color.
examples: The bright moon lit up the whole field.
Bright stars filled the sky on the clear night.
She painted her room a bright shade of green.

easy.def: Very bright.
examples: The sun is brilliant.
A brilliant light.
The brilliant colors.

more.def: Very bright and shining.
examples: The brilliant sun made me squint.
Fireworks lit the sky with brilliant colors.
The diamond sparkled with brilliant light.

easy.def: Very smart.
examples: A brilliant idea.
She is brilliant.
He had a brilliant plan.

more.def: Extremely clever or smart.
examples: She came up with a brilliant idea.
He is a brilliant scientist.
The detective had a brilliant plan.

easy.def: To carry something to a place.
examples: Bring your book.
She brought her lunch.
I will bring a toy.

more.def: To carry or lead someone or something to a place.
examples: Please bring your homework to school on Monday.
My aunt brought flowers when she came to visit.
Can you bring the baby her blanket?

easy.def: Wide.
examples: The river is broad.
He has broad shoulders.
The broad road has four lanes.

more.def: Wide from one side to the other.
examples: The broad river was too deep to cross.
The football player had broad shoulders.
A broad path led to the gate.

easy.def: A boy who has the same parents as you.
examples: My brother is tall.
I play with my brother.
Her brother is five.

more.def: A boy or man who has the same parents as another person.
examples: My older brother taught me how to throw a ball.
She has two brothers, and they love to build forts.
His little brother follows him everywhere.

easy.def: Having the color of chocolate or dirt.
examples: My dog is brown.
Bears have brown fur.
The tree trunk is brown.

more.def: Having the color of soil, wood or chocolate.
examples: The brown leaves crunched under our feet.
She packed her lunch in a brown paper bag.
A brown owl sat quietly in the tree.

easy.def: The color of chocolate or dirt.
examples: Brown is my favorite color.
Mix red and green to make brown.
The cat is mostly brown.

more.def: The color of soil, wood or chocolate.
examples: The room was painted in shades of brown.
Autumn fills the woods with orange, red and brown.
Her eyes are a warm brown.

easy.def: A tool with stiff hairs on a handle.
examples: I use a brush to paint.
Brush your teeth.
The brush is wet.

more.def: A tool with hairs, bristles or wire on a handle, used to clean, paint or tidy things.
examples: She dipped the brush in blue paint.
He used a hair brush to fix his hair.
I cleaned the pot with a stiff brush.

easy.def: To clean something by rubbing it with a tool.
examples: I brush my teeth.
She brushed her hair.
He brushed the dog.

more.def: To clean, smooth or paint something by rubbing it with a tool that has stiff hairs.
examples: I brush my teeth twice a day.
She brushed the dust off her coat.
He brushed the horse until its coat shone.

related.def: Small bushes and plants growing under tall trees.
